title: Patatas Bravas (Crisp Potatoes with Spicy Tomato Sauce and Garlic Mayonnaise)
summary: Crisp-roasted potato chunks are topped with a smoky, gently spiced tomato sauce and a cooling garlic mayonnaise for a classic tapas bar favourite. The contrast of textures and flavours makes it a popular sharing dish.

ingredients.item: floury potatoes (such as russet or Maris Piper), peeled and cut into 2.5 cm chunks
garlic cloves, grated to a paste
fine sea salt or table salt
garlic cloves, grated to a paste

steps.title: Start the bravas sauce
steps.text: Warm the oil in a small saucepan over medium-low heat, then add the garlic, paprika and cayenne and cook for about 30 seconds until fragrant. Keep the heat gentle here, as paprika scorches and turns bitter within seconds if the pan is too hot.

steps.title: Build the sauce
steps.text: Stir in the tomato purée and cook for 30 seconds, then add the water and simmer for 4-5 minutes until thickened to a loose, spoonable sauce.

steps.title: Finish the sauce
steps.text: Take the pan off the heat and stir in the vinegar and salt, then set aside to cool. Adding the vinegar at the end keeps its sharp edge rather than cooking it away.

steps.title: Make the garlic mayonnaise
steps.text: Stir the mayonnaise with the grated garlic and lemon juice until smooth, then set aside.

steps.title: Heat the oven and tin
steps.text: Preheat the oven to 230°C (210°C fan) at least 20 minutes ahead, with the oil already in the roasting tin so it's hot by the time the potatoes go in.

steps.title: Parboil the potatoes
steps.text: Boil the potato chunks for 1-2 minutes in water with the bicarbonate of soda and salt, then drain and shake them in the colander to roughen the surfaces. The alkaline water softens the potato's outer layer slightly, which gives a craggier, crunchier roast later.

steps.title: Roast
steps.text: Tip the potatoes into the hot oil in the tin, turning to coat, and roast for 20 minutes.

steps.title: Turn and finish roasting
steps.text: Turn the potatoes and roast for a further 15-20 minutes until deep golden and crunchy on all sides.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Pile the potatoes onto a plate, spoon over the bravas sauce and drizzle with the garlic mayonnaise. Serve hot with cocktail sticks for easy sharing.

tips: Keep the paprika over gentle heat for only a few seconds — it burns and turns bitter very quickly if the pan is too hot.
Don't skip roughening the potatoes after parboiling; this is what gives them a craggy surface that crisps up properly in the oven.
Make sure the oil in the tin is properly hot before adding the potatoes, or they'll stew instead of roast.
Spoon the sauce and mayonnaise on just before serving so the potatoes stay crisp rather than going soggy underneath.
storage: The sauce and mayonnaise can be made up to 2 days ahead and kept covered in the fridge. Potatoes are best roasted and eaten fresh, as they lose their crunch on reheating; if needed, reheat in a hot oven at 220°C (200°C fan) for 8-10 minutes until piping hot and crisp again before adding the sauce. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
